name: Introduction to Arraylists
html:
Welcome back dear reader. So, are you enjoying the coding journey so far? You have already learnt a lot and there is still a lot to learn. You have been using arrays for a while now. You have already learned about 1-D arrays and 2-D arrays and you have practiced some problems on them. Now, it's the time to introduce you to something called Arraylist. It is another data-structure, just like an array (but very different). In Java, the developers have written a class for Arraylist and it's methods. Therefore, it is also called the "Arraylist class" many times. (Don't worry about classes, if you don't know what they are. We will study them under object-oriented Java programming).You may watch the INTRODUCTION TO ARRAY LIST VIDEO for an overview of Arraylists first, then we will move together into this article and explore Arraylists in a little depth.


Important Links : Introduction Video


Watch video What is an Arraylist?

Let's talk about an array first. What is an Array? We say that it is a data-structure, which is a collection of similar data-types which are arranged in a contiguous memory. Given below is an image of an array: (see fig-1)

As you can see in fig-1, we have been given an array of size=5. The fact that it has contiguous memory is shown by memory addresses of each index at the bottom of the array. The base address of the array is 201 and the size of Integer data-type is 4 bytes. Thus we can see each element taking 4 bytes of memory and there is no break between 2 consecutive elements. The first element, present at index 0 ends at memory address of 204 and the second starts at 205, without any gaps in between. This happens in the entire array and so the memory is contiguous. You know all this already, right? So, why are we studying it again? We are studying it again because the arraylist also follows all these rules. It will also have a contiguous memory but, there is a difference. Look at the fig-1 carefully once again. We have written A[5] which means an array of size 5. So, we have to define the size of an array for creating an array in the memory. But, we do not have to define the size of an Arraylist. This is the major difference between an array and an arraylist. Now, what do we exactly mean when we say we do not need to define the size of an arraylist? Well, the size is automatically adjusted by the arraylist. We can enter as many elements as we want, the arraylist will manage the size by it-self. (Obviously "as-many" also has a limit of the memory).

How an Arraylist Works?

Have a look at the image given below:

There is something called as Size and Capacity. Size of an array or an Arraylist is the number of elements that are currently present in it and the capacity is the total number of elements that can be present inside the array/Arraylist. The size of the above Arraylist was 5 and the capacity was also 5. So the array list was complete. But, we wanted to insert 52 in the Arraylist. How will that happen? As we already told you, the array list manages the size itself. It actually doubles the total capacity of the list. So the current capacity was 5, when 52 was inserted, the capacity became 10 and after the insertion of 52 there are still 4 spaces vacant for insertion.

Note that the capacity doubles only when there is no space for insertion. Look at the diagram given below:

After 52 we inserted 45,36,54 and 92 and the Arraylist did not expand as the capacity was enough to store all those elements. When we entered 7, the total capacity doubled again, and became 20. Similarly the capacity will not expand on entering 9 more elements. Note: The initial size of Arraylist is 0 as it is empty and the initial capacity of an Arraylist in Java is 10.

Arraylist Declaration:

Now it's the time to see Arraylist working in code. We can declare an Arraylist as follows:

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); //declares an integer arraylist Arraylist< String> a2=new Arraylist < >(); //declares an arraylist of string } }
java; true";

Similarly, we can declare an Arraylist for various data-types. We recommend you to write code simultaneously so that you don't make any mistakes in the Syntax.

Size() of an Arraylist

We can get the size of an Arraylist by using its size() function. Since the list is empty, the size will be displayed as 0.

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); //declares an integer arraylist Arraylist< String> a2=new Arraylist < >(); //declares an arraylist of string System.out.println(a1.size()); } }
java; true"; Add() in Arraylist

The add() function adds an element at the end of the list. We can also add the element at a particular index using add() function.

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); //declares an integer arraylist Arraylist< String> a2=new Arraylist < >(); //declares an arraylist of string System.out.println(a1.size()); a1.add(10); a1.add(20); a1.add(30); a1.add(1,1000); //Adds 1000 at index 1 }}
java; true";

Display an Arraylist:

There are various methods to display an Arraylist. We can display it using loops as well as directly using the System.out.print() .

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); //declares an integer arraylist Arraylist< String> a2=new Arraylist < >(); //declares an arraylist of string System.out.println(a1.size()); a1.add(10); a1.add(20); a1.add(30); System.out.print(a1); //prints the entire list at one go for(int x:a1) { System.out.println(x); //each element belonging to a1 will get printed } } }
java; true";

Get() in Arraylist

For getting the value at a particular index in Arraylist, we use the get function.


import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); //declares an integer arraylist Arraylist< String> a2=new Arraylist < >(); //declares an arraylist of string System.out.println(a1.size()); a1.add(10); a1.add(20); a1.add(30); System.out.print(a1); //prints the entire list at one go for(int x:a1) { System.out.println(x); //each element belonging to a1 will get printed } int val=a1.get(1); //gets the value at index 1 System.out.println(val); for(int i=0;i< a1.size();i++) { System.out.println(a1.get(i)); //printing using get() } } }
java; true";

Set() in Arraylist

For changing the value at a particular index we use the set() function.



import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); //declares an integer arraylist Arraylist< String> a2=new Arraylist < >(); //declares an arraylist of string System.out.println(a1.size()); a1.add(10); a1.add(20); a1.add(30); a1.add(1,1000); // adds 1000 at index 1 System.out.print(a1); //prints the entire list at one go for(int x:a1) { System.out.println(x); //each element belonging to a1 will get printed } int val=a1.get(1); //gets the value at index 1 val=10; for(int i=0;i< a1.size();i++) { System.out.println(a1.get(i)); //printing using get() } a1.set(1,2000); //changes the value at index 1 to 2000; } }
java; true";

Remove() in Arraylist

Remove() function is used to remove an element from a particular index.

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n = scn.nextInt(); ArrayList< Integer> al = new ArrayList< >(); //declares an integer arraylist Arraylist< String> a2=new Arraylist < >(); //declares an arraylist of string System.out.println(a1.size()); a1.add(10); a1.add(20); a1.add(30); a1.add(1,1000); // adds 1000 at index 1 System.out.print(a1); //prints the entire list at one go for(int x:a1) { System.out.println(x); //each element belonging to a1 will get printed } int val=a1.get(1); //gets the value at index 1 val=10; for(int i=0;i< a1.size();i++) { System.out.println(a1.get(i)); //printing using get() } a1.set(1,2000); //changes the value at index 1 to 2000; a1.remove(1) //removes the value at index 1 } }
java; true";

So dear reader, these were some of the basic methods of Arraylist. We have a lot of other methods, but we don't use them all. We will study other methods whenever we encounter them. We hope you got a basic understanding of Arraylist and how it is different from Arrays.


Suggestions:

Some suggestions from our side that you don't want to miss:

  1. This is the first time that you have studied Arraylist. So, revise it once more either by watching INTRODUCTION TO ARRAYLISTS video or by reading the article again. Watch video
  2. Just reading the article or watching the video or even practicing the syntax is not enough at all. You will get a good hold of the concepts and the syntax when you practice some problems. So, revise this topic and quickly move to our next question i.e. REMOVE ALL PRIMES. Happy coding!!
